_comment: posse's fork of herdr-bob's shipped rules.json (ranger-base-0sa5a).
Upstream's file matches NONE of Bob 2.0.5's three blocked screens and DOES
match one of its idle screens -- MEASURED 2026-10-03 against the six
captures in etc/herdr/agent-detection/upstream/bob/ by
scripts/verify-herdr-bob-rules.sh, which replays them through the plugin's
OWN match_rules. The false positive is the serious half: the `/` command
picker lists `/permissions - View and change this folder's trust level`,
which satisfies trust_folder_prompt's `all` (`trust`) and its `any`
(`this folder`), so an idle composer with the picker open reports blocked
and every wait on that pane stops.
bob-watch seeds this file into config_root() once and never refreshes it,
and prefers it over the plugin's own copy, so this is an override that
needs no write to the managed checkout. Installed by
scripts/herdr-bob-rules.sh --install; sent upstream as
etc/herdr/agent-detection/upstream-herdr-bob-rules.md.
THE TWO MEASURED RULES COME FIRST, and they are ports of posse's own draft
herdr manifest for Bob (etc/herdr/agent-detection/upstream/bob/bob.toml),
which already keyed on exactly the right lines -- the patterns existed, in
the wrong file. Each is a PAIR of line-anchored patterns on two different
lines, never a shared footer: `Press Enter to confirm` is the Execute
Command dialog's footer and nothing else's today, but codex's hooks_review
rule exists because a footer reword silently returned a blocked screen to
idle (rangerhq-7ia). grep matches per line, so two patterns that cannot
share a line are a two-line anchor.
NO MULTIBYTE CHARACTER IN A BRACKET EXPRESSION -- use alternation.
MEASURED 2026-10-03: /usr/bin/grep (BSD grep 2.6.0-FreeBSD) under LC_ALL=C
evaluates `[>❯→]` byte-wise, so it matches a pure box-drawing line (`─` is
E2 94 80 and the class degenerates to the byte set {>, E2, 9D, AF, 86,
92}); `(>|❯|→)` does not, in any of the four grep x locale combinations
tested. It changes no verdict in upstream's file today, because its class
is followed by a required keyword -- but the watcher does not choose which
grep or which locale it gets, and a daemon started from launchd has no
LANG at all.
trust_folder_prompt and license_prompt remain UNFIXTURED: no capture in the
corpus shows Bob's trust or licence screen, so their positive side is still
upstream's guess and is left as upstream wrote it apart from the narrowing
that fixes the picker. What IS pinned about them is negative and checkable:
they must match none of the six.
Rules are matched, in order, against the bottom of the pane buffer; the
first match wins, so the precisely-named rules are first and the log line
says which screen was recognised. `all` entries must every one match; `any`
needs one; `none` must not match. POSIX extended regexes, case-insensitive.

rules._why: Bob 2.0.5's Execute Command approval dialog. Keyed on the heading and the selected option. The heading alone is not enough: a COMPLETED call leaves ' Execute Command (completed)' in the scrollback, which the anchored pattern excludes and which blocked-execute-command-scrollback.txt pins -- that capture carries both spellings and must still resolve here. The row marker is optional on purpose: the dialog being up is the block, not which row the cursor sits on.

The browser sign-in screen. A bob with no usable gateway token draws this INSTEAD of a composer -- there is nothing beneath it, and Esc or Ctrl+C exits the program, so no key posse is willing to press can clear it. Anchored on both lines: the first alone could plausibly appear as a notice over a live composer in some future build, the pair cannot.

Upstream's generic approval rule, kept as the net under bob_execute_command. Matches no capture in the corpus. Two changes from upstream: the row-marker bracket expression is now an alternation (see the locale note above), and U+2192 is in it, which is what Bob 2.0.5 actually draws.

UNFIXTURED. Narrowed from upstream's `(trust|do you trust)`, whose bare `trust` alternative matched `/permissions - View and change this folder's trust level` in the command picker -- a false blocked on a live composer. This asks for the question form, which is upstream's own other alternative; nothing is invented here.
UNFIXTURED, and unchanged from upstream: no capture in the corpus contains `licen[sc]e` at all, so it cannot fire on one.

Upstream's generic sign-in rule, kept as the net under bob_signin. Two changes: the hyphen, because Bob writes `sign-in` and upstream's `sign in` therefore matched nothing in blocked-signin.txt -- the second miss in the shipped file; and `press enter` is dropped from `any`, because it is the Execute Command dialog's footer too (MEASURED: present in both execute-command captures), which is a shared footer doing identifying work.
